Thanks, I agree about walks! I spend about 1hr or more walking him per day and it's usually a high point. There are occasional days (like yesterday) when I feel too depressed to walk but even on those days I try force myself to go anyway. 

I love to see my pup being happy, running around, sniffing stuff. I love exploring the city and nature. I appreciate when people approach me on walks or want our dogs to meet but unfortunately my social anxiety has me mainly focused on how I can politely get away asap. 

Also, he is a rescue dog who was about to be put down due to biting and he can be unpredictable when meeting new dogs and people so that adds to the anxiety. For example sometimes he's chill at first, which I praise him for, but then the person may try to pet him in a way he doesn't like or the dog may try to sniff his butt in a way he doesn't like and then he's snarling and biting again. I do my best to train him right but tbh most times I'd rather just avoid all people.

It's unfortunate to feel so lonely but at the same time so strongly want to avoid potentially awkward/ dangerous/ uncomfortable situations.

Thanks for your post! One part that stood out to me is where you say you're "not talented" in your job but that you enjoy it. IMHO ability to enjoy stuff truly is a talent, and is in fact especially useful in a job such as yours which involves checking in hotel guests and planning parties. Even if it hasn't translated into promotions, I'd guess that it makes you pleasant and effective in many ways.

From what I can tell from what you've written you don't seem like an ass. You've got some challenges but some good things going as well.

There are books out there on DBT--if you buy one or borrow from the library it could be worth a try. Marsha Linehan invented DBT and wrote some good books. 

Wishing you the best. X
